newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Widows takes a shine to multi-utilities.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Widows takes a shine to multi-utilities.

text.p: Scottish Widows Investment Management said on Thursday it would continue to shy away from UK utilities in general, but it found the concept of multi-utilities appealing.
The company, which has 22 billion stg under management, said utilities suffered from an unpredictable blend of politics and regulation.

"(But) the multi-utility concept offers its customer base a more complete package of services -- such as those offered by Scottish Power and United Utilities -- and we like that," managing director Leslie Robb said.
In the long run, utility share prices will always be determined by political and regulatory interference.

"The long-term share price performance of British Gas and British Telecom...has been particularly unimpressive," he said. "History suggests that the water and electricity companies are going to be no different, particularly if a Labour government is about to take office."
Current levels of dividend payouts to electricity shareholders are unlikely to be sustained.
"At some point most stocks will get back to being valued for what they really are -- dull, uninteresting, regulated utilities," Robb said.
"We only want to back well-managed companies which can grow top-line sales in a regulated environment."
